Senses.Explanation: Literally, "seal" (印) and "approve or permit" (可): "approve and certify," attested 761 times in 173 allowlisted texts. Lamp and lineage records use the verb for recorded acts of approval. After a student opens to understanding at Tianyi's assembly, Tianyi "approves him, saying: this is my house's thousand-mile colt" (印可曰，此吾家千里駒也). Another account says a teacher approved six people individually and told them, "you six people together verify my body; each accords with one part" (汝等六人，同證吾身，各契其一). Narrative forms include "all received approval" (皆蒙印可), "deeply received approval" (深蒙印可), and "received the teacher's approval" (承師印可). These passages record approval, the teacher's words at approval, and who received it; they do not make every occurrence a single theory of what was certified.
Senses.Note: Approval is not always the end of examination. In the Zhang Shangying case, after Donglin has approved the commissioner, Doushuai asks whether he still has any doubt about the words and teachings of buddhas and ancestral teachers. Historical notices also distinguish a person's approving teacher from the lineage teacher ultimately named in succession: one person can receive approval from more than one teacher while a later record names a particular succession relation. The headword records the approval event; lineage assignment remains a separate structural claim.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衣印可曰：此吾家千里駒也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tianyi gives approval and calls the student his house's thousand-mile colt.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師各印可曰：汝等六人，同證吾身，各契其一。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A raised lineage account: the teacher approves six disciples individually and says each accords with one part.

Occurrences.Kwic: 謁汾陽、葉縣，皆蒙印可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Biographical narrative: the student visits Fenyang and Yexian and receives approval from both.

Occurrences.Kwic: 東林既印可運使，運使于佛祖言教有少疑否？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Doushuai asks: since Donglin approved the commissioner, does the commissioner still have any doubt about the words and teachings of buddhas and patriarchs?

Occurrences.Kwic: 謁金鑾善、葉縣省，皆蒙印可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A second multi-teacher narrative: visits to Jinluan Shan and Yexian Sheng both result in approval.

Senses.Explanation: Chan records load the ordinary printing block into a criticism of sayings and conduct reproduced from fixed models. One record asks, 'what is block-stamped?' and answers: people who grope along walls, have no genuine understanding of their own, and rely entirely on ancient sayings as a staff. Another defines 'printing-block Chan' as reading the records of Yuanwu, Dahui, and Zhongfeng and turning out something resembling them. The widespread paired formula says that teachers or learned sayings are 'stamped from a printing block and released from a mold,' then contrasts this with responding as circumstances arise. The Zen deviation is this printing-shop language for publicly criticized, model-bound Chan speech; the term does not merely mean generic sameness.
Senses.Note: Primary Zen-loaded sense. Family checked against mold (模子), printing-block Chan (印板禪), stamped from a printing block (印板上打來), and released from a mold (模子裏脫出).

Occurrences.Kwic: 印板禪印板禪何謂印板？有等靠墻摸壁，自無真正見解，全藉古人言句做拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Direct definition formula: reliance on ancient sayings without one's own genuine understanding.

Occurrences.Kwic: 印板禪者，熟讀圓悟、大慧、中峰諸尊宿語錄，依稀脫出者是也；
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Definition within a three-part taxonomy: producing a resemblance after reading masters' records.

Occurrences.Kwic: 而今天下老和尚多是師承學解，露布葛藤，印板上打來，模子裏脫出。當人若是明去，何不一切臨時？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The recurring printing-block/mold formula contrasted by the text with acting as circumstances arise.

Senses.Explanation: The physical engraved block used to print a text. One colophon records carving a set of printing blocks for the Continued Transmission of the Lamp, comprising three cases. An imperial instruction orders Zhongfeng's writings printed and entered into the canon wherever canon printing blocks are held. This book-production object is a different thing from speech criticized as block-stamped, so it has its own sense.
Senses.Note: Literal object sense, independently attested in a printing colophon and an imperial book-production record. No specifically Chan bend belongs to this physical sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 彫造續燈錄印板一部，計三函。時崇寧二年十月日謹題。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Colophon recording an engraved printing-block set for the Continued Transmission of the Lamp.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但有藏經印板處。教刊板入藏經。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperial instruction to carve and print the text wherever canon printing blocks exist.

Senses.Explanation: Literally "different kinds." In Chan questions it can stand alone: asked "what are the other kinds?" (如何是異類), one master strikes a bowl and calls a servant to eat, while another answers "the foot is short, the inch is long" (尺短寸長). Its defining Zen deployment is the fixed expression "move among other kinds" (異類中行). Nanquan says people of the time must move among other kinds; challenged on "kind," he puts both hands on the ground. Another witness places the expression beside "although moving in an animal's conduct, one does not receive an animal's recompense" (雖行畜生行，不得畜生報). Cao Dong's record supplies the sharpest lexical boundary: the ancients provisionally borrowed the water buffalo as an "other kind"; it is an other kind in the matter, not an other kind in language (古人權借水牯牛為異類。秖是事上異類。非言語中異類). The entry records these answers and boundaries without deciding what spiritual condition they express.
Senses.Note: Count: 745 occurrences in 194 allowlisted texts; "move among other kinds" (異類中行) has 268 occurrences in 103 texts. Cross-check against the existing "move among other kinds" entry was mandatory. The standalone noun and the noun inside the fixed expression retain the same referent, so item 8 does not warrant a split. The separate longer entry remains the proper home for the full formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是異類。師敲椀曰。花奴花奴喫飯來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A direct what-is question receives an action and a call to the servant; the record supplies no prose gloss.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是異類？師曰：尺短寸長。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A second direct question receives the answer 'the foot is short, the inch is long.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 今時人。須向異類中行始得。師曰。異即不問。如何是類。泉以兩手拓地。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Nanquan's public exchange: the longer formula is challenged at the word 'kind,' and Nanquan puts both hands to the ground.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人權借水牯牛為異類。秖是事上異類。非言語中異類。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Cao Dong's record explicitly identifies the borrowed water buffalo and distinguishes the matter from verbal classification.

Occurrences.Kwic: 道箇如如早是變了也。今時師僧須向異類中行。歸宗曰。雖行畜生行。不得畜生報。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The formula is transmitted with Guizong's animal-conduct response and Nanquan's criticism.

AlternateTargets: going among other kinds of beings
Senses.Explanation: Literally, to go among different kinds of beings, especially animals. The phrase is shared vocabulary across Chan records and is repeatedly posed as a public question. A verse says that one who is like geese passing through the sky and leaving no intended trace can go among the different kinds; a list of teaching-house essentials makes it the tenth requirement for continuing the teaching line. Nanquan joins the phrase to becoming a water buffalo and answers a question about the kinds by putting both hands on the ground. A separate witness connects his use with the warning that speaking where knowing does not reach makes horns grow. Caoshan's record pairs going among the different kinds with the matter among the different kinds, and a later Caodong formulation places it within the three falls. These passages establish influential Nanquan and Caodong deployments, but they continue to name going among the different kinds rather than different master-owned referents.
Senses.Note: The headword has 268 hits in 103 allowlisted texts. Earlier drafting split Nanquan and Caodong menus from the corpus-wide phrase and supplied interpretive targets such as acting where knowing cannot reach. Item 8 rejects that structure: the records attach the same phrase to different exchanges and technical clusters, but do not define separate things. The entry therefore keeps one corpus-wide sense and reports the master-specific evidence in its explanation, occurrence notes, roster, and related terms.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鴈過長空。影沉寒水。鴈無遺蹤之意。水無留影之心。若能如是。方解向異類中行。不用續鳧截鶴。夷嶽盈壑。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse on going among the different kinds, credited here to Tianyi Yihuai and circulated in other records.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉示眾曰：喚作如如，蚤是變了也。今時師僧須向異類中行。歸宗曰：雖行畜生行，不得畜生報。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Guizong responds to Nanquan's statement by speaking of performing an animal's conduct without receiving an animal's recompense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 九、須大機大用。十、須向異類中行。凡欲紹隆法種，須盡此綱要，方坐得這曲彔床子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Going among the different kinds appears as the tenth item in a list of essentials for continuing the teaching line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 泉曰。山前檀越家作一頭水牯牛去。師曰。謝師指示。泉曰。昨夜三更月到牕。泉曰。今時人。須向異類中行始得。師曰。異即不問。如何是類。泉以兩手拓地。師近前一踏。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Nanquan joins the phrase to the water-buffalo exchange and responds to the question about the kinds with an action.

Occurrences.Kwic: 巖不薦，卻問泉：「智頭陀為甚不袛對和尚？」泉曰：「他卻是異類中行。」巖曰：「如何是異類中行？」泉曰：「不見道：『智不到處切忌道著，道著即頭角生。』直須向異類中行。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An independent witness connects Nanquan's phrase with the warning about speaking where knowing does not reach.

Occurrences.Kwic: 謂如南泉曰。智不到處切忌道著。道著則頭角生。喚作如如。早是變也。直須向異類中行道取異類中事。洞山曰。此事直須妙會。事在其妙。體在妙處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Caoshan's record cites Nanquan and pairs going among the different kinds with the matter among the different kinds.

Occurrences.Kwic: 隨緣放曠，任運逍遙，披毛戴角，是類墮；解向異類中行，不斷聲色，是隨墮；彼師所墮，汝亦隨墮；不受食，是尊貴墮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later Caodong formulation places the phrase within the three falls.
